Commentary.Commentary: That brings us to the close of a hard-fought contest. Ireland will be pleased that they got through but they have to learn to be more responsible. Another slip might have cost them the match. Afghanistan, on the other hand, need to improve their batting. We are all set to have an edge-of-the-seat finale. Join us for all the action on 31st August at 1045 local (0945 GMT). Till then, cheers!

Ireland skipper, William Porterfield says that it was a very good performance from them. Mentions that in the previous ODI series in Sharjah against Afghanistan in 2017 as well, they lost the first game and had bounced back after that. Credits Simi Singh for batting well and taking his side through. Praises his bowlers for being on the money. States that they were disappointed as they failed to get over the finish line in the previous game. Admits that it would have been good if they had won with 10-15 overs to spare but is relieved that they won this game. Ends by saying that he anticipates a close battle in the decider.

Afghanistan skipper, Asghar Afghan says that they played well in this game. Feels that they were around 25-30 runs short but he is happy with the way his boys played. States that the wicket was not difficult and they needed to perform better.

The man of the moment, Andy Balbirnie, is being interviewed on the sidelines. He says that they needed a win like this after the last game. States that it would have been nice if he remained not out. Mentions that he enjoys playing for Ireland and feels that it will be a close game again on Friday.

However, Simi Singh showed great temperament and a calm head on his shoulders as he took the hosts past the finishing line with some useful support from Tim Murtagh, who managed to hold his fort for 11 deliveries.

Rashid Khan then dismissed Andy Balbirnie to put the cat among the pigeons. The tourists could smell an upset as their spinners were looking threatening. At one stage, Ireland were 164 when they lost their seventh wicket in the form of Andy McBrine.

The wily leggie, Rashid Khan, then got into the act, trapping Kevin O'Brien in front. However, Andy Balbirnie dug in hard and came up with a well-crafted half century giving the Irish chase some direction. Simi Singh gave him apt support as the two put on a 47-run stand to take the home team within 39 runs from victory.

A win at last for the home team, a deserving one at that. They just about scratched their way home in the end. After a shaky start, losing Porterfield in the very first over, Ireland crawled their way back into the chase with a handy 69-run partnership between Paul Stirling and Andy Balbirnie. It was smooth sailing until the most experienced player from the visiting team, Mohammad Nabi, struck twice, dismissing Stirling and Niall O'Brien.

That's it! Ireland hold their nerves to get over the finishing line! Tossed up ball outside off, Murtagh leans ahead to block but gets an outside edge that rolls towards third man. Two runs taken. The Irish camp is all smiles. IRELAND WIN BY 3 WICKETS WITH 37 BALLS TO SPARE!
Full on leg stump, worked off the inner half towards short fine leg.

Five Wides! That will probably do for Ireland! Nabi bowls an arm ball but it is going down the leg side. Murtagh tries to flick but misses. Shahzad should have collected it but gets beaten and the ball rolls to the fine leg fence.
Nabi continues to bowl short. Simi stands tall and places it to sweeper cover for a single. Ireland need 7 more.
Similar delivery, the shorter length allows Singh to camp back and punch it out towards covers.
On a flatter trajectory, kept out watchfully.
Mohammad Nabi is back. Can he pick up a wicket to put more pressure on the opposition?

Big shout for LBW, turned down! Mujeeb is not happy. He feels he had his man. He keeps it full on off, Murtagh comes forward to turn it into the leg side. The ball pitches and spins away from Tim, beats his bat and brushes his front pad before going behind. There is a strong appeal from the bowler and the fielders but the umpire shows no interest. The replay shows that it was probably missing the off stump. Good call. A good spell from Mujeeb ends. He finishes with figures of 10-0-41-1.

Not Out! He's safe. Beautifully bowled by Mujeeb. He gives this one some flight and keeps it full on off. Murtagh is dragged forward, out of his crease, as he tries to push at the ball. It turns away after pitching and beats the bat. Shahzad behind the stumps takes the bails off in lightning fast speed and feels he has got his man. The square leg umpire goes upstairs. Replays show that Murtagh's back foot is just about inside the crease, or has he been given the benefit of the doubt? After several replays, the third umpire decides it is not out but that was very close though.
This is going down to the wire! Another lightning piece of stumping by Shahzad. His body language suggest that Murtagh is a goner. Let's find out...
Strays on his pads, Singh flicks it wristily towards the square leg region and adds a run to the total.

Mujeeb fires it just outside off, Singh waits back and opens the face of the bat at the very last moment. The ball flies past the slip fielder. The man at short third man though chases it down and keeps it down to two.
Tossed up on the middle stump, pitches and spins away slightly. Singh takes the spin into account and defends well.
Leg Bye! Full and down the leg side, Murtagh tries to flick it but the ball hits his pads, rolls down towards the short fine leg region and the batsmen take a single.
Leg Bye! Short ball, rising on Murtagh. He goes for the pull but misses. The ball hits him on the helmet and lobs to the vacant short fine leg region. A single taken.
Similar delivery, played off the inner half of the bat down the track.
Full ball outside off, Murtagh plays it with soft hands back towards the bowler.
Back of a length outside off, eased through cover-point for an easy run. Ireland need 13 more.
Sensible from Tim! This is what he needs to do, give the strike to Singh. He waits on the back foot and turns this length ball through mid-wicket for a single.
Wide! Alam switches his angle to round the wicket but slips this one down the leg side as Murtagh misses his flick.
Full toss on off, hit away towards deep backward square leg for a run. The batsmen think about the second but the fielder swoops in to deny them.

Big appeal for LBW, not given. Rashid keeps it full on the stumps, Murtagh tries to turn it into the leg side but misses. Rashid and his team go up for an LBW appeal but the umpire replies in the negative. Rashid is bowled out now. He finishes with figures of 10-0-37-3.
Keeps it full on off, Singh drives this nicely to long on for a single.
Singh gets forward to this tossed up delivery on off and defends solidly.
Fires this one on the pads, Murtagh flicks it away with a wristy shot towards deep square leg for a single.

OUT! We have a match on our hands! Suddenly the Afghanistan tent is alive. Rashid keeps it very full on the off stump. McBrine comes forward to defend. The ball pitches and turns in to beat the front foot block, or it seemed to have beaten it. The ball then hits his front pad and up go the visiting team. The umpire has no doubt as he raises his dreaded finger. But McBrine does not look happy as he is seen shaking his head vigorously while walking back. Replays show there was a faint inside edge before the ball hit the pads. Lucky break for Afghanistan. Will this help them crawl back in the match?
McBrine gets back to this shortish one and blocks it down the ground.
Wide! Bowls this wide down the leg side and the umpire stretches both his hands out to signal the extra.
Tim Murtagh is the new man in.
Time for Powerplay 3! Maximum of five fielders are now allowed outside the 30-yard circle till the end of the innings.
Back of a length outside off, McBrine taps it towards covers for a run and gets off the mark.
Pitched up ball outside off, pushed off the front foot towards mid off.
Fullish ball in line of the stumps, eased towards mid on.
Andy McBrine is the new man in.

OUT! Bowled 'em! Gary Wilson must be absolutely gutted with himself. There is no demand to take such a risk when you are so close to victory. He has given Afghanistan a sniff. Coming back to the ball, Alam spots Wilson shuffling across his stumps and hence, bowls a full and fast ball on leg. Gary tries to get some bat on it but the ball sneaks through and crashes into the stumps. There certainly seems to be a twist in the tale, I can smell it.
Similar length ball outside off, kept out watchfully.
On a length around off, defended solidly off the back foot.
Alam is back.
Khan keeps it tight on the off stump line. Singh gets behind the line of the ball and blocks it out.
Singh defends this tossed up delivery off the front foot.

FIVE WIDES! Ireland will accept this gift gleefully. Khan fires this one in, strays a bit down the leg side. It is a fast googly as the ball pitches and spins past the pads and the keeper can't stop it. It runs away fine to the boundary. Rashid is not happy.... 5 extra runs conceded.
Drives this full pitched delivery to the fielder at extra cover. No run on offer.
Fuller on the off stump, Singh drives it nicely to covers but cannot find the gap. No run.
Wilson gets on his knees and sweeps this full ball to the fielder at deep square leg for a single.
Tossed up delivery on middle is driven to the long on region for a single.
Rahman bowls it a bit straight, Singh waits in his crease and works it towards the square leg region for a single.
Full and straight ball is driven to mid on for a single.
Keeps it full on off, Wilson gets hit on the pad. Big appeal goes up but neither the bowler nor the umpire are that interested.
Comes forward and defends this straighter and fuller ball into the off side. No run.
Tossed up around off, Wilson gets right behind the ball and blocks it out.
Wilson defends this fuller ball on off back to the bowler.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
There is the spin threat of Rashid Khan and Mujeeb Ur Rahman which this pair needs to see off. This is an interesting phase of play.
Slips in a googly on middle and leg, Singh tries to flick it away but misses. The ball brushes his pads and rolls to the man at 45.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
This one pitches outside off and skids after landing, Singh lets it go.
Straighter one from Rashid, Simi gets behind it and blocks it solidly.
Quicker and on a fuller length around off, Wilson places it towards point for a quick single.

SIX! How good is that from Singh! He dances down the track, gets to the pitch of this one and smashes it over the long on fence. The power and timing is exquisite which takes the ball over the rope for a maximum. What an important hit for Ireland!
A bit shorter and wider, Wilson goes back and punches it through the cover region for a single.
Gets on the front foot and blocks out this full delivery on middle and off.
Fuller on off stump. Comes forward and defends it solidly.

Risky single taken. Pushes this length ball into the cover region and takes off for a single. The fielder there is quick to pick it and throw at the non-striker's end. He misses the stumps and the replay shows that Singh was out if it would have hit. Close call.
Tossed up on off, Singh prods forward and defends.
Fuller and straighter, defended back to the bowler.
Gary Wilson comes out to bat. Ireland only need 39 to win from 91 balls with five wickets in hand but they have to bat sensibly. A slip here might land them in trouble.

OUT! Rashid, the dangerman strikes. Do we still have a match on our hands? Rashid keeps it full outside off, Balbirnie leans forward and goes for the big booming drive. Does not reach the pitch of the ball but still goes through with the shot. The ball lands and turns away sharply, taking the outside edge and flies to first slip, where Zadran does brilliantly to dive to his left and latch on to this sharp chance. Can Afghanistan make further inroads?
Pulls the length back a bit and fires it on the leg stump, Singh goes back and flicks it to the deep square leg region for a single.
Rashid continues to keep it just outside off, goes back and punches it to deep point for a single.
Seems like Andy Balbirnie has hurt his forearm. He slipped while taking the single and landed awkwardly. He looks in pain and the physio attends to him.
Singh waits back to this flighted delivery on off, taps it towards the point region to get a single.
Tossed up on off, Singh stays in his crease and defends.
Wide. Rashid slides this one down the leg side. Wide given.
Rashid Khan returns.

FOUR! Perfectly swept by Balbirnie and he gets a pressure relieving boundary for the hosts. Nabi keeps it very full just outside off. Andy gets down on his knees, gets out the sweep shot. He times and places the ball perfectly as it beast the fielder at the deep square leg fence for a boundary.
Tossed up ball, driven nicely through mid on for another single.
Nabi keeps it on a length in the line of the stumps, Andy flicks it wristily into the mid-wicket region, they run a single.
Nabi pulls the length back a bit, Singh rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball through covers for a single.
Tossed up on off, defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Nabi continues with his tight line and a fullish length. Singh taps it to mid-wicket.
Nabi is back.
Strays onto his pads, Singh flicks it to long leg, a run is added.
Defended by getting right behind the line of this full pitched ball on off.
Pushes this one to the cover fielder. No run.
Dances down the track again, gets to the pitch this time and lofts it over the extra cover region. Two runs taken.
Beaten! Singh cannot pick this carrom ball. It pitches on off and turns away ever so slightly beating Singh's outside edge.
Singh skips down the track, sees that he's not to the pitch of the ball, decides to defend at the last moment.
Shortish ball from Naib is pulled into the square leg region for a single.

A back of a length delivery outside off. Singh goes after this wide one and misses completely. Easy take for the keeper behind the stumps as he goes up with a strong appeal. The umpire shows no interest in the appeal. No edge there.
Fullish ball outside off is driven through covers. It is timed well but the diving fielder at covers does well to save three.
A short of a length ball on off, seems to have stopped a bit after pitching. Andy waits for it to arrive and defends well.
The length ball is blocked well in the gap on the off side, they run through for a quick single.
Starts with a length ball angling in, Singh tries to drive through the line, gets a thick inside edge and the ball runs down to the deep square leg fielder for a single.
Full and outside off, squeezed away to deep point for a single.
Tossed up ball in line of the stumps, swept away to short fine leg for a single.
Tossed up around off, Andy comes ahead and taps it to the covers.
The batsman has driven it straight down the ground.

7th ODI fifty for Andy Balbirnie! Back-to-back for him in this series. He has a matured head on his shoulders. Floated outside off, Balbirnie strokes it through covers to come back for a brace. He raises his bat and gets a good round of applause from the scanty crowd. He will be aiming to guide his team through to the finishing line.
Tossed up around off, defended solidly off the front foot.
Mujeeb Ur Rahman comes back for a bowl.
Fractionally overpitched outside off, creamed to sweeper cover for a run.
Just a touch fuller in the off stump corridor, Andy punches it on the up towards mid off.
On a length outside off, glided away calmly to third man to rotate strike.
Similar delivery outside off, this time it is punched through cover-point for an easy single.
Brilliant work from Najibullah! Short and some room on offer, Balbirnie slaps it hard towards backward point. Zadran stationed there flies to his left and stops a certain boundary.
On a length around off, pushed off the back foot towards mid off.
Naib returns for a bowl.
Flighted on middle and off, Singh stands back in his crease and defends.
Tossed up outside off, Singh leaves it alone.
There is now some discussion going on between the the Afghanistan skipper and umpire Ian Gould. He is telling him to calm down.

Beaten! Was there an edge though? A lot of drama here. This one has landed full outside the off stump, Singh comes forward to push it to the off side but the ball pitches and spins past the outside edge. Shahzad takes it and appeals as he feels there was a nick there. The visitors keep appealing but do not get any response. The Afghanistan skipper, Afghan has some words to say to Simi. He looks angry but don't think there is any reason to react like that. The umpire's call is always the final call. The replays show the ball just brushed the flap of his back pad before entering into the keeper's gloves. Ireland need to guard against the threat of Rashid.
Tossed up delivery on off, Simi comes forward and defends it.
Khan flights this one on the middle and leg stump line, Andy flicks it away wristily for a single towards square leg
Quicker and a bit shorter on off, Singh goes back and taps it into the covers region for a single.

Two Leg Byes! Alam fires it a bit straighter, Andy tries to flick it, the ball clips his pad and rolls through square leg. Balbirnie turns quickly and just beats the throw back into the keeper. Two Leg Byes result.
FOUR! Crashed! Alam keeps it short this time. Andy rocks back and pulls this perfectly in the gap between deep square leg and deep mid-wicket.
Single skips down the track and drills this fullish delivery down the ground for a single.
Shorter in length in line of the stumps, Andy pulls it to the fielder at the deep square leg fence, they cross over for a single.
A bit short of a length, shaping in to the batsman, Singh flicks it to the deep square leg region for a single.
Fuller delivery on off,  driven to wide mid off, diving stop by the mid off fielder keeps them to a single.
Andy taps this length ball towards point and takes a quick single.
This short of a length delivery has been cut away through square on the off side. No run of offer.
Beaten! Fuller and slower on off, Andy tries to put bat on ball but misses.
A bit slower on middle by Rashid, Singh picked it early and slog swept it through the leg side. One run added to the total.

FOUR! Streaky boundary! Rashid is a bit unlucky as he bowls a quicker one just around off, Singh goes for the drive but gets an outside edge. The speed of the ball is too much for the slip fielder as the ball races to the boundary.
Keeps it just outside off, punched to the deep point fielder for a single.
Ends the over with a fuller ball on off. Singh drives but drives straight to the fielder at covers.
Alam pulls the length back a little, Andy waits on the back foot and punches it to the cover-point region for a single.
Quick single. A back of a length delivery angling in, Singh turns it round the corner for a single.
Fuller and straighter on off, Simi comes forward and defends it back to the bowler.
Similar delivery just wider of off is punched to the fielder at covers.
He's right on the money first ball, keeps it on a length just on off stump. Singh stays back in the crease and defends it down the pitch.
Alam returns.
Full on middle, nudged away to short fine leg for a run. A wicket and 6 from the over.
That was risky! Rashid spots Singh moving across his stumps and hence, he bowls it quick on middle. Simi just manages to defend it. Was a clear candidate for LBW if he missed it.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Outside off, played with the spin to point.
Wide! Down the leg side, Singh fails to flick it away.
Simi Singh strides out to bat.

OUT! Rashid Khan strikes! This was coming, you can always expect a wicket around the corner when the magician is bowling. He slips in the googly and it is pretty quick in pace as well. O'Brien camps back in order to read it off the pitch but he is late to bring his bat down. Is hit flush in front of the stumps and Rashid and Co rise up in a vociferous appeal. The umpire obliges as well. Looked pretty adjacent to the naked eye. The visitors are well and truly heading back into the contest. The hosts need 86 from 154 balls while Afghanistan need 6 wickets.

DROPPED and FOUR! O'Brien is a lucky man! Quicker outside off, O'Brien pushes at it but gets an outside edge behind. It deflects off Shahzad's gloves, brushes the fingertips of the diving Nabi and runs to the fence behind. Was a difficult chance but you need to snap everything when you have a low score to play with.
Change of ends for Rashid Khan.
Continues to keep it back of a length, O'Brien goes for the pull and picks up a single at deep square leg.
Kevin rocks onto the back foot and punches this shortish ball to the fielder at covers. Dot again.
A short of a length delivery has been cut away through square on the off side. The batsmen cross over for a single.
On a length around off, driven into the covers and it is stopped by the fielder. No run.
On a length outside off, Andy tries to cut it past the short third man fielder but cannot find the gap.
Kevin pushes hard at this short of a length delivery on off. The ball rolls down towards covers. They take a single.
Nabi bowls it fuller on the middle stump line. Kevin wrists this towards the mid-wicket region and picks up a single.
Gives it a bit more flight. Andy reaches to the pitch of the ball nicely and drives it through covers for an easy single.
Andy comes forward and blocks out this full ball on the stumps.
O'Brien punches this shortish flighted delivery into the cover region. They run a single.
Beaten! Kevin tries to block this full ball, it does not spin and skids straight. Beats Kevin's outside edge and he is beaten on the very first ball. Pressure on!
Kevin O'Brien strides out to bat.

OUT! Timely wicket for the tourists. The most experienced player in the Afghanistan team is turning things around, picks up his second wicket. Nabi floats this one on a full length just around off. O'Brien makes a bit of room and drives it hard but he is unable to keep it down. Unfortunately for Niall, he picks the substitute fielder, Shafiqullah at extra cover perfectly who takes an easy catch. Will this open the floodgates for the visiting team?
Length ball on off, O'Brien does well to steer it to the third man region. Yet another single results.
A bit shorter outside off by Naib. Andy goes on the back foot and punches this towards the cover region for a single.
Keeps it on a length just outside off. O'Brien waits for the ball to arrive, opens the face of his bat at the very last moment and glides it to the third man region for a single.
Goes back and flicks this straight ball to the square leg region for a single.
A length ball on off, Andy gets his head right on top of the ball and defends with a full face of the bat.
Naib fires it on the batsman's pads, O'Brien glances this one away to fine leg for a single.
Gulbadin Naib is back on.
Defends this flighted delivery on off back to the bowler.
This is tight stuff from the experienced campaigner. Tosses this up in line of the stumps. Balbirnie prods forward and defends.
Beaten! A bit quicker, flatter and wide of off stump, Andy goes for the cut but misses it completely.
Tossed up on the off stump, punched back to Nabi.
Similar delivery again, this time he leans forward and blocks it down.
Tossed up ball on off, defended back to the bowler.
Time for Drinks!
O'Brien drives this full delivery to mid off. No run on offer.
This flighted ball on off is tapped away towards point.
Tossed up delivery on off, driven to the cover region, they cross for a single.

A bit on the shorter side, Andy goes back and whips it to deep square leg, calling for a couple. The fielder runs in quickly and throws at the striker's end but it is a wayward one. The batsmen have run two, but it could have been tight if the throw was a bit closer to the stumps.
Uses his wrists this time to work this flighted one towards the mid-wicket region for a single.
Quicker one on off, O'Brien stays back and punches it to point.

Leg Bye! Tossed up ball hits the batsman low on the pads as he tries to whip it across the line. The ball trickles down towards square leg region and one run added to the total. A leg bye signaled by the umpire.
Niall tries to turn it away with the angle on the leg side but the fielder at short fine leg does well to attack the ball and denies the single.
Balbirnie stays back to this flighted delivery on middle, flicks it to the square leg region and picks up a single.
Niall gets forward to the pitch of this full length delivery and flicks it to mid-wicket to pick up a single.
Tossed up ball is tapped to the point region.
FOUR! Nabi fires it down the leg side, it sits up nicely for O'Brien as he sweeps the ball past the short fine leg fielder for a boundary.
Slower and flighted on the middle and off line, Andy comes forward and defends.
Tossed up ball on the off stump, O'Brien leans forward and drives it down the ground for a single.
Googly again, but beaten this time. Rashid pulls back his length and keeps it a bit slow. Niall tries to push at the ball but the away turn beats his outside edge.
Googly this time just outside off, read well by Niall O'Brien who lunges forward and defends it to covers.
Full toss outside off, driven to the sweeper cover fielder for a single.
Flatter delivery darted on the middle and leg stump, Andy goes back to whip it into the leg side but misses it and the ball hits his pads. That was going down the leg side.
Slower through the air, defended solidly off the front foot.
Tossed up ball, flicked away towards square leg.
Quick and in line of the stumps, kept out off the inner half of the bat.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Niall O'Brien is the new man in.

OUT! Yes, the milestone man has taken a step in the right direction. A very, very important breakthrough for Afghanistan! A wonderful piece of bowling from Nabi has done the trick. He floats this one around off and the ball drifts away. Stirling uses his feet and pushes at it but it goes on with the arm and beats him. Shahzad behind the stumps is lightning quick and takes the bails off in a flash. The Afghanistan players are celebrating but the umpire refers it upstairs. They are checking for the front foot no ball which is fine. After that, it is being seen whether Shahzad collected the ball in front of the stumps while affecting the stumping. Well, he seems to be fine on that count too. Stirling has to make his way back. An entertaining knock from him ends. Ireland need 114 from 202 balls.
Nabi comes from around the wicket and bowls a tossed up ball, Stirling comes forward and blocks it.
Full ball on middle, tucked to short fine leg.
There is a bit of a break. Shahzad has taken a blow on his chin and takes a bit of a breather. Meanwhile, the players sip on some water.

Was there an edge? Maybe not. Fullish ball outside off, spinning away. Balbirnie goes for the drive but seems to have missed it. Shahzad fails to collect it properly. The replay indicates that the bat might have hit the ground.
Almost a replica of the previous delivery as he leans ahead and taps the tossed up ball towards mid-wicket.
The wrong one from Rashid, Balbirnie reads it well and tucks it with a closed bat face to mid-wicket.
Driven towards the mid on region. They pick up a single.

A chirpy appeal for an LBW is turned down! Straighter one on off, skids after landing. Stirling tries to work it away but is hit on the thigh pad. Khan is confident but the umpire stays put. The replay shows that it was pretty high.
Time for Rashid Khan. Can the spin magician make his presence felt?
Shorter one on off, punched off the back foot to the covers.
Outside off, placed towards short third man.
Stirling comes forward to the fullish ball and strokes it through covers for a single.
Quick and flat outside off, Stirling goes for a cut but gets beaten.
On a flatter trajectory, Andy hangs back and punches it through point to rotate strike.
Pushed quicker through the air outside off, dabbed away with soft hands to the cover region.
Balbirnie waits for the length ball and dabs it to third man for an easy run. He will retain strike.
On a fuller length around off, Andy shuffles across and works it off the inner half towards mid-wicket.
Full ball in line of the stumps, eased back to the bowler.
Overpitched outside off, stroked nicely to sweeper cover for a single.
Stirling is flowing like a river at the moment! Walks down the track to the fullish ball and flicks it through wide mid on to pick up a couple.
On a length in the off stump corridor, played with an angled bat to the point region.
Quicker one outside off, cut away nicely to sweeper cover for a run.
This one doesn't turn much as Paul comes ahead to dead-bat it.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.

That could have been close! Low full toss, Balbirnie drives it back towards Nabi. The bowler knows what he is doing as he tries to deflect it off his hands towards the stumps at his end but can't do it cleanly. Well, if he was able to do so, Stirling would have been a goner as the replay indicates.
Short and there is a lot of width, cracked away against the spin to deep point for a run.
The batsman has driven it through mid on. They pick up a single.
Fractionally overpitched outside off, drilled but can't beat the man at extra cover.
Full and in line of the stumps, eased towards mid on.
Full ball around off, kept out watchfully.

Good game awareness from the duo! Ireland have been right on the money throughout in this game. Fullish ball, angling in, tucked off the inner half towards square leg. There are huge vacant spaces there and they hare back for the second.
Full ball attacking the stumps, driven towards mid on for an easy run.
Pitched up ball around off, Balbirnie is early into his flick and gets a a leading edge which falls well short of mid off.
Short and room on offer, Stirling flashes his blade at it but misses. 8 from the over.

SIX! What a blow! That was clean as a whistle. Tossed up delivery, Stirling lines it up, skips down the track and smokes it over long on for a huge maximum. Picked the bones out of that one. That brings up the 50-run stand between the duo. They are on the right track.
Played to mid-wicket region by the batsman.
Straighter one from Nabi, Stirling plays for the spin but misses.
Fuller in length, swept away through square leg for a run.
On middle and leg, turned around the corner for a single.

Time for Powerplay 2! Four fielders are allowed outside the 30-yard circle now till the 40th over. Meanwhile, Mohammad Nabi to roll his arm over now. He didn't have a good outing with the bat but can he turn things around with the ball in his 100th ODI?
FOUR! Cracking stroke! On a driveable length outside off, Balbirnie leans ahead, opens his bat face and caresses it behind point to find the fence.
Very full outside off, played off the outer half of the bat to third man for a single.
Pitched up ball, eased off the front foot to mid off.
Close shave! Balbirnie works this fuller length ball towards mid on and takes on the fielder. He has a shy but misses. Could have been interesting had he hit.
Very full ball, well outside off, squeezed out towards the point region.
Starts off with a yorker, a good surprise delivery first up. Balbirnie is switched on as he defends it nicely to the off side.
Gulbadin Naib comes into the attack.
Leans ahead to the floated ball and blocks it down the track.
Another brisk run! Balbirnie drives it towards wide mid off and scurries to the other end.
Quick but it is short which allows Paul to go back and place it towards mid-wicket for a quick run.
The carom ball from Mujeeb. Stirling reads it correctly and blocks it under his nose.
Straighter in line and shorter in length, defended with a straight bat.
Spinning into Andy who works it through mid-wicket for a single.
Slower ball around off, Stirling comes forward and dead-bats it.
Full ball on off, kept out watchfully.
FOUR! Delightful! Fractionally overpitched outside off, Stirling's eyes light up as he strokes it through covers for another boundary.
Pitched up ball around off, eased to covers.

Great work from the young Mujeeb! Shortish ball on off, Stirling pulls it hard through square leg. Rahman in the deep hares to his left and slides full length to keep the ball in play. Saves a couple for his side.
FOUR! Sit and applaud! That was brilliant to watch! Length ball outside off, Stirling with a high elbow and a good head position drills it through covers. There is no stopping that one.

Shoddy stuff from the visitors! They do not have a big target to defend and every run matters. Stirling plays this one with the spin through mid-wicket for a run. A poor throw from the fielder at the keeper's end and Shahzad had no chance to stop it. There is no one to back up as well and a couple of overthrows result.
Played to mid-wicket region by the batsman. They pick up a single.
FOUR! Nicely done! Full ball on middle and leg, Balbirnie kneels and sweeps it past the keeper. It is very fine and runs to the fence behind.
Paul makes use of the depth of the crease to turn this one through mid-wicket to rotate strike.
A touch shorter, going straight on. Paul defends it down the track.
Floated just outside off, defended solidly off the front foot.
Straying on the hips, nudged with ease to fine leg for a brace. 7 from this over.
Camps back to the back of the length ball to block it.

FOUR! A shot of a man who is in good form! He played an organized knock in the previous game and his team needs him to replicate his efforts. Fullish ball outside off, swinging in. Balbirnie leans ahead and strokes it with authority through covers to pick up his first boundary.
Length ball on middle, keeps a touch low. Balbirnie does well to adjust in his crease and works it to mid-wicket.
Pitched up ball around off, pushed with soft hands to the off side.

Another shout for an LBW but to no effect! On a length around off, nipping in. Stirling shuffles a touch and walks down the track in order to flick it but misses to get pinged on the pads. Alam rises up in an appeal but gets no response from the umpire. The replay shows that the impact might have been just outside off.
Full and loopy ball on middle and off, Andy strides forward to knock it down to mid on.
The ball hits the batsman low on the pads. The batsmen have run through for a single. A leg bye signaled by the umpire
Rahman errs on the leg stump again, Andy has no problem in tucking it around the corner to rotate strike.
A bit slower in pace and straighter in line, helped away with the spin through mid-wicket for an easy run.
Leans ahead to the loopy ball and brooms it away through square leg to rotate strike.
Balbirnie is nimble on his feet as he drives the tossed up ball to wide mid off.
Length ball on a stump-to-stump line, Paul gets behind it and stonewalls it.
Stirling needs to find the gaps! Back of a length ball and there is width on offer, Stirling punches it with good timing but once again picks out Rashid.
Good shot but for no run! Length ball outside off, Stirling comes ahead confidently and opens his bat face to cream it nicely but finds Rashid Khan at point.
Length ball, straying on the hips, turned around the corner for a single.
Back of a length ball, Andy camps back and blocks it with a straight bat.
Full length ball attacking the stumps, kept out defensively towards short mid-wicket.

An appeal for an LBW falls on deaf ears! Googly from the back of the hand, Stirling leans ahead to defend but the ball spins in to go past his defense and hits him on his pads. Rahman shouts for it but the umpire stays put. Perhaps going down leg.
On a flatter trajectory, Stirling keeps it out watchfully.
Paul camps back to the shorter one and keeps it out.
FOUR! Shot! That's the first boundary of the innings! Straighter one from Mujeeb outside off, skids after landing. Stirling drives it through covers to find the fence.
Slower through the air, drifting in, Stirling comes down the track but is not quite to the pitch of it. Ends up chipping it wide of the man at mid on for a brace and gets off the mark.
Tossed up around off, Stirling puts his head down and defends it calmly.
Beaten! On a driveable length outside off, Andy goes for a booming drive but misses. Alam begins with a maiden.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Well bowled! This one comes back in sharply from a length outside off. Balbirnie hangs back and punches it to the covers.
Full ball around off, driven crisply to the man at mid off.
Good length ball in the tight off stump corridor, Andy hangs back and blocks it stoutly.
On a length outside off, shaping away, Balbirnie points his bat skywards to allow it through.
Aftab Alam to bowl from the other end with the second new ball.
Andy Balbirnie is off the mark. Picks it off his pads and flicks it away behind square leg for a single. End of a terrific over from the offie Mujeeb.
Keeps it around off from over the wicket now, blocked with the full face of the bat.
Andy Balbirnie walks in at no.3.

OUT! Perfect start for Afghanistan! A wicket in the very first over of the game, much like how the first innings went. This was expected in the second innings, Ireland will just have to deal with it. Mujeeb bowls it short and in line of the stumps from around the wicket, but the ball keeps extremely low, almost goes underground really. Nothing William Porterfield can do about it as he goes miles under his bat and crashes into the stumps. First one down for the hosts.
A bit on the shorter side, around off, Porterfield forces it to covers off the back foot.
Another one quicker through the air, safely guarded out.
Fuller and around off, Porterfield blocks it off the front foot.

We are back for the chase. Not going to be easy for Ireland by any means. A slow wicket which is about to get slower and they will face the Afghan spinners. It is poised to be a good second half. Mujeeb Ur Rahman will take the new ball, while William Porterfield and Paul Stirling will start for Ireland. Here we go...
